summary: Over the 14-day analysis period, the user achieved a 121.6 mg/dL average glucose with 98.7% sensor coverage and active closed-loop automation. The strategy relies 100% on Unannounced Meals (UAM) with zero logged carbohydrates. While daytime glucose management is mostly stable, there is a recurring pattern of severe nighttime and early morning hypoglycemia (up to 18.5% time below range at 01:00) driven by aggressive reactive insulin delivery against delayed digestion.
issues: Severe late evening and early nighttime hypoglycemia (10-18.5% Time Below Range between 00:00 and 03:00).
Excessively high safety limits (Max IOB of 25 U, Max Basal of 12 U/h) that remove practical guardrails for the algorithm.
A mismatch between the rapid reactive insulin delivery of the UAM algorithm and the delayed gastric emptying typically associated with the user's GLP-1 medication.
Nighttime targets of 90 mg/dL leave no margin of safety against late-acting insulin stacking.
education: GLP-1 medications slow gastric emptying, meaning food takes much longer to absorb into the bloodstream.

When a loop algorithm relies purely on Unannounced Meals (UAM) without knowing meal sizes or duration, it interprets early post-meal glucose rises as strong resistance and may deliver large amounts of insulin rapidly.
Max IOB (Insulin On Board) and Max Basal limits are critical safety parameters that prevent the loop from delivering too much insulin at once when it miscalculates future glucose trends.
strengths: Excellent sensor wear time with 98.7% coverage and minimal gaps.
Consistent and active use of the AAPS closed-loop system.
Overall Time in Range (86.0%) is very strong, indicating the baseline profile and automation handle fasting conditions well outside of meal events.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
The current Max IOB setting of 25 U represents roughly 125% of the total daily insulin dose (approx. 20 U/day) and poses an acute risk for severe hypoglycemia.
Modifying automation limits should be prioritized over base profile changes to establish a safe baseline.

analysis_steps.findings: Sensor coverage is excellent (98.7%). Telemetry and profile data are fully present. However, there are exactly 0 logged carbohydrate entries, indicating a pure UAM approach.
analysis_steps.evidence: Gap count is 10; valid_entry_count is 3995. treatment_summary.carb_entries is 0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of carbohydrate entries prevents traditional Carb Ratio (CR) evaluation or precise meal absorption modeling.

analysis_steps.findings: There is a significant and recurring risk of hypoglycemia during the evening and nighttime. Local hourly Time Below Range reaches 15.3% at 19:00, 11.4% at 00:00, and 18.5% at 01:00.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local data shows severe TBR spikes late in the day; glucose_extremes logs multiple events between 41-45 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot differentiate fasting hypos from late meal insulin stacking due to lack of meal timing data.

analysis_steps.findings: Nighttime targets are set aggressively low (90 mg/dL at 00:00 and 23:00). Combined with active UAM and SMB, the system aggressively corrects any lingering meal rises, frequently overshooting the target.
analysis_steps.evidence: Target segments show 90 mg/dL at 23:00 and 00:00. Loop status telemetry shows active SMBs driving glucose down.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Base basal rate accuracy is masked by constant SMB/UAM activity.

analysis_steps.findings: ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U and DIA is 10 hours. CR values exist (10.5 - 13.2 g/U) but serve only as mathematical weights for UAM since carbs are never logged.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True CR performance is invisible without logged meals.

analysis_steps.findings: The system is fully dependent on UAM with a rapid 3-minute SMB interval and smb_always_enabled. It reacts instantly and heavily to unannounced rises.

Max IOB (25 U) and Max Basal (12 U/h) are set to dangerously high levels given the user's estimated 20 U TDD. This allows the UAM algorithm to stack massive amounts of insulin against delayed GLP-1 meal spikes, causing the severe nighttime crashes.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_settings.raw_settings show max_iob_units=25.0 and max_basal_u_per_hour=12.0. Loop logs show 120m glucose drops of up to -178 mg/dL following large automation-driven temp basals.

analysis_steps.findings: The user relies on a 100% reactive Unannounced Meal strategy with zero proactive bolusing.
analysis_steps.evidence: treatment_summary shows 0 carb entries and 0 total carbs.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific meal behaviors, compositions, and timing.

analysis_steps.findings: The combination of GLP-1 delayed digestion, pure UAM reliance, and practically uncapped Max IOB/Basal limits is the root cause of the severe nighttime hypoglycemia. These limits must be restricted, and the nighttime target raised, before adjusting any base profile values.
analysis_steps.evidence: Integration of extreme limits (25U IOB) with 18.5% TBR at 01:00 and zero logged carbs.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing carb data restricts deeper optimization, but the safety hazard is clear without it.

recommendations.title: Restrict Max IOB and Max Basal Limits
recommendations.description: The current safety limits allow the system to front-load massive amounts of insulin in response to delayed meal spikes, directly causing severe nighttime hypoglycemia. These limits should be restricted to better align with the daily total dose.

recommendations.title: Raise Nighttime Glucose Targets
recommendations.description: A target of 90 mg/dL overnight leaves no safety buffer against late-acting insulin stacked by the UAM algorithm. Raising the target will reduce the aggressiveness of nighttime microboluses.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The 90 mg/dL nighttime targets at 23:00 and 00:00 offer insufficient safety margins against UAM-induced insulin stacking, contributing to the severe 11-18% Time Below Range observed in the early morning hours.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight Time Below Range for 3-5 days after raising the target and restricting AAPS safety limits.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the target segments at 00:00 and 23:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100-110 mg/dL.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Current limits are extraordinarily high (25 U IOB vs ~20 U TDD) and allow the algorithm to dangerously front-load insulin against delayed GLP-1 meal spikes.
Dynamic ISF is functioning as designed, but its output must be capped by the recommended lower Max IOB limits.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Introduce basic carbohydrate logging, even without an immediate prebolus, to provide the loop with duration context for the delayed GLP-1 digestion.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: A pure UAM strategy reacts only to the immediate glucose rise. With delayed digestion (GLP-1), the algorithm front-loads insulin assuming a standard meal, causing that insulin to peak before the food absorbs, driving extreme lows.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether logging estimated e-carbs (without upfront bolus) smooths the automation delivery and reduces severe post-meal and nighttime crashes.

implementation_steps: First, restrict AAPS Safety Limits: Reduce Max IOB and Max Basal to values appropriate for the total daily dose (e.g., 5 U and 3 U/h) to stop massive automated insulin dumps.
Second, raise the nighttime glucose targets at 00:00 and 23:00 from 90 mg/dL to at least 100-110 mg/dL to build in a safety margin.
Observe overnight Time Below Range for 3-5 days to ensure the severe hypoglycemia is eliminated.
Discuss introducing simple carbohydrate estimates (e-carbs) for dinner to give the algorithm visibility into the extended digestion timeline caused by the GLP-1 medication.
